topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening framing welcomes students, introduces the lecture series structure, and outlines the foundational learning outcomes for cancer biology.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of genetic regulation, differentiation, and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a multi-step disruption of normal cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization driven by accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes, alongside the laboratory models used to study it.

topics.label: Tumour invasion, metastasis, and progression from benign to malignant disease
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how tumors invade local tissue, spread to distant organs, and evolve through a stepwise continuum from benign precursor lesions to invasive malignancies.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature and classification conventions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard suffix-based naming rules and clinical exceptions used to classify benign and malignant neoplasms across different tissue lineages.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the anatomical, systemic, and metastatic processes by which primary and secondary tumors impair normal physiology and cause patient death.

topics.label: Tumour incidence across human tissues and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the prevalence and tissue distribution of cancers in human populations with patterns observed across diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical screening modalities and early cancer detection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the diagnostic principles, histological bases, and practical challenges of population screening programs for identifying pre-invasive and early-stage cancers.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical session reminders
topics.groupedBecause: The closing framing reiterates the core learning outcomes and directs students to upcoming practical classes and subsequent lectures.
